Rules B3/S23

How many live neighbours (out of 8) a cell needs.

Born (dead cell comes alive)
Survives (live cell stays alive)

How to play

  1. Tap or drag on the board to draw some live cells.
  2. Press Play (or Step for one generation at a time).
  3. Drop in a pattern, or tick different boxes to invent a new rule.

What's happening?

  • Every square is a cell. It's alive (bright) or dead (dark).
  • Each step, every cell counts its 8 neighbours. That's all it looks at.
  • Conway's rule, B3/S23: a dead cell with exactly 3 live neighbours is born. A live cell with 2 or 3 survives. Everything else dies.
  • From those tiny rules you get blinkers, gliders that crawl away, and guns that fire gliders forever. Nobody programmed those in.
  • The board wraps: walk off one edge and you come back on the other.

Try this: drop in an R-pentomino (just 5 cells) and press Play. How many generations until it calms down? Then switch to HighLife (add B6) and try again.
